entities.summary: Enrique de Guzmán y Ribera, 2nd Count of Olivares was a Spanish nobleman and statesman who played a crucial role in the politics of Southern Europe during the Early Modern period. He was a key figure in the Spanish royal court and served as a diplomat, military commander, and administrative official. His influence extended to the Catholic Church, with which he collaborated closely. The Count of Olivares was a prominent advocate for the interests of the Spanish monarchy and worked tirelessly to maintain the country's power and influence in Europe. He was also a patron of the arts, supporting prominent artists and writers of his time. The Count's legacy is marked by his efforts to modernize Spain's institutions and promote the growth of its economy. Despite his significant contributions, the Count's impact on the world stage was somewhat limited by the complexities of the Spanish monarchy's internal politics. The Count's life and career serve as a testament to the enduring power of the Spanish royal court during this period. His influence can still be felt in the modern-day politics and culture of Southern Europe.

entities.summary:
Enrique de Guzmán y Ribera, 2nd Count of Olivares was a Spanish nobleman and statesman born on March 1, 1540, in Madrid, Spain.

He played a key role in the Spanish Habsburg administration, serving as Viceroy of Spain from 1579 to 1580 and Governor-General of New Spain from 1581 to 1585.

Guzmán's policies aimed to maintain Spanish dominance in the Americas and strengthen the royal authority in the region.

His legacy includes the establishment of the Olivares dynasty, which ruled the province of Salamanca, and the development of the Spanish Inquisition's policies in the New World.

"The conquest of the New World was a great undertaking, but it was not without its challenges and controversies." - Enrique de Guzmán y Ribera, 2nd Count of Olivares
